title: feat(search): add fzf-style fuzzy matching (matcher, filter, quick-open demo)
body:
## Summary
Add fzf-style fuzzy matching to @floatboat/nexus-plugin-search (roadmap #17):
a matcher engine, a ranked list filter, and a fuzzy quick-open in the demo.

## Motivation
- Roadmap (docs/ROADMAP.md): #17 Fuzzy search (P2), "evaluate fzf-like algorithm
  vs. third-party lib". Built in-house — no new dependency.

## Changes
- `packages/plugin-search`:
  - `fuzzyMatch` — score one candidate (subsequence match + positions).
  - `findFuzzyMatches` — line-by-line document search, ranked, absolute offsets.
  - `fuzzyFilter` — rank an arbitrary list (key/limit); the quick-open building block.
  - First README for the package.
- `apps/electron-demo`:
  - Fuzzy quick-open panel (Ctrl/Cmd+P): filter vault by path, highlight matches,
    arrow-nav, Enter to open. Built on `fuzzyFilter`; no extra IO.
- `docs/ROADMAP.md` + `.zh.md`: #17 → done.

## Testing
- [x] `pnpm test` — 553 tests pass (20 new: fuzzy + quick-open)
- [x] `pnpm build` — all 11 packages build (ESM + d.ts); demo renderer bundles
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean

## Compliance
- AI disclosure: functional code written with AI assistance (Claude); design,
  fzf algorithm choice, and scoring reviewed and defensible.
- New dependencies: none.
- [x] No build artifacts / secrets committed.

commits_at_first_review.message:
feat(search): add fzf-style fuzzy matching utilities

Implements roadmap item #17. Fuzzy matching answers a different question
than exact/regex search: does the query appear as an in-order subsequence,
allowing gaps? This is the model behind quick-open, symbol pickers, and
command palettes.

Built in-house (no new dependency) following fzf's FuzzyMatchV1: a
forward + backward scan narrows each candidate to the shortest window that
still contains the query, then a single linear pass scores it. Ranking
rewards contiguous runs, word/camelCase boundaries, and the first
character, and penalizes gaps.

- `fuzzyMatch(text, query, options?)` scores one candidate, returning the
  matched character positions (or null when there is no subsequence match).
- `findFuzzyMatches(doc, query, options?)` fuzzy-searches a document line
  by line and returns matches ranked best-first, with absolute document
  offsets ready to drive a highlight or "jump to match".

Shipped as pure utilities (like the existing findSearchMatches /
replaceAllMatches) rather than wired into the Cmd/Ctrl-F panel, since
@codemirror/search has no fuzzy mode and grafting one in is a separate
concern. Adds the package's first README documenting the search plugin
and the fuzzy API.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(search): add fuzzyFilter for ranked candidate lists

Layer a generic list filter on top of fuzzyMatch — the building block for a
quick-open dialog, command palette, or symbol picker. Non-matching items are
dropped; the rest are ranked best-first, ties broken by original order.

- `key` extracts the string to match from object items.
- `limit` caps the result count after ranking.
- Unlike findFuzzyMatches, an empty query returns every item (input order,
  score 0) so a picker can show the full list before the user types.

Each result carries the original item plus the match positions (into the
item's own text) for highlighting. Documented in the package README.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(electron): add fuzzy quick-open (Ctrl+P) to the demo

A floating file picker that fuzzy-filters the vault by relative path, ranks
matches best-first, highlights the matched characters, and jumps to the chosen
file. Opens with Ctrl/Cmd+P or the toolbar button; ArrowUp/Down to navigate,
Enter to open, Esc to close.

Built entirely on the plugin-search fuzzy API (`fuzzyFilter`), demonstrating
the engine capability end-to-end. Files come from the existing in-memory
LinkIndex and open through the same path as wiki-link navigation, so no extra
IO or IPC is added.

The picker is a self-contained renderer module with an ARIA listbox and a
jsdom-driven test covering filter/highlight/keyboard-nav/select/empty states.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

+# @floatboat/nexus-plugin-search
+
+Search & replace for [Nexus-Editor](https://github.com/floatboatai/Nexus-Editor) —
+an accessible CodeMirror 6 search panel plus a set of pure, editor-independent
+matching utilities.
+
+- **Drop-in panel** — `createSearchPlugin()` wires up `Cmd/Ctrl-F` with a
+  headless, ARIA-labelled find/replace UI (case, regexp, whole-word toggles).
+- **Search query history** — opt-in, host-injected storage (no implicit
+  `localStorage`); recall with `ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown`.
+- **Pure matching utilities** — `findSearchMatches` / `replaceAllMatches` run on
+  a plain string, so hosts can build their own search UI, count matches, or
+  batch-replace without mounting the panel.
+- **fzf-style fuzzy matching** — `fuzzyMatch` / `findFuzzyMatches` for
+  quick-open, symbol pickers, and command palettes.
+
+## Install
+
+```bash
+pnpm add @floatboat/nexus-plugin-search @floatboat/nexus-core
+```
+
+## Quick start
+
+```ts
+import { createEditor } from "@floatboat/nexus-core";
+import { createSearchPlugin } from "@floatboat/nexus-plugin-search";
+
+const editor = createEditor({
+  container: document.getElementById("editor")!,
+  initialValue: "# Hello\n\nStart typing...",
+  plugins: [
+    createSearchPlugin({
+      top: true,
+      highlightSelectionMatches: true,
+      history: true // opt-in; pass { storage } to persist
+    })
+  ]
+});
+```
+
+Press `Cmd/Ctrl-F` to open the panel. `createSearchPlugin` returns a
+`NexusPlugin` — pass it straight to `createEditor`.
+
+### Panel options
+
+| Option | Default | Notes |
+|---|---|---|
+| `top` | `true` | Render the panel above the content (vs. below). |
+| `caseSensitive` | `false` | Initial state of the case toggle. |
+| `highlightSelectionMatches` | `true` | Highlight other occurrences of the current selection. |
+| `history` | `false` | `true` enables in-memory history; `{ storage, storageKey?, maxEntries? }` persists it. |
+| `labels` | English | Override any panel string (i18n). |
+
+## Matching utilities
+
+These are plain functions over a string — no editor instance required.
+
+### `findSearchMatches(doc, query, options?): SearchMatch[]`
+
+Exact / regexp / whole-word matching. Returns every match as
+`{ from, to, text }`. Invalid regular expressions return `[]` rather than
+throwing.
+
+```ts
+import { findSearchMatches } from "@floatboat/nexus-plugin-search";
+
+findSearchMatches("foo bar Foo", "foo", { caseSensitive: false });
+// [{ from: 0, to: 3, text: "foo" }, { from: 8, to: 11, text: "Foo" }]
+
+findSearchMatches("v1 and v2", "v\\d", { regexp: true });
+// [{ from: 0, to: 2, text: "v1" }, { from: 7, to: 9, text: "v2" }]
+```
+
+### `replaceAllMatches(doc, query, replacement, options?): string`
+
+Returns a new document with every match replaced. `SearchOptions` are shared
+with `findSearchMatches`: `{ caseSensitive?, wholeWord?, regexp? }`.
+
+## Fuzzy matching
+
+Fuzzy matching answers a different question than exact search: *does the query
+appear in the text in order, allowing gaps?* This is the model behind editor
+quick-open, symbol pickers, and command palettes — type `fzm` and match
+`f`uz`z`y`M`atch.
+
+### `fuzzyMatch(text, query, options?): FuzzyMatchResult | null`
+
+Scores a single candidate. Returns `null` when `query` is not a subsequence of
+`text`, otherwise `{ score, positions }` where `positions` are the indices of
+each matched character (ascending). Higher scores are better matches; scores are
+only meaningful relative to each other.
+
+```ts
+import { fuzzyMatch } from "@floatboat/nexus-plugin-search";
+
+fuzzyMatch("live-preview-table.ts", "lpt");
+// { score: 65, positions: [0, 5, 13] }  ← l(ive) p(review) t(able)
+
+fuzzyMatch("hello", "world");
+// null
+```
+
+An empty query is a zero-score match (`{ score: 0, positions: [] }`). Matching is
+case-insensitive unless `{ caseSensitive: true }` is passed.
+
+### `findFuzzyMatches(doc, query, options?): FuzzyMatch[]`
+
+Fuzzy-searches a document line by line and returns the matching lines ranked
+best-first. Each `FuzzyMatch` carries **absolute document offsets** so the
+result can drive a highlight decoration or a "jump to match":
+
+```ts
+interface FuzzyMatch {
+  from: number;      // offset of the first matched char
+  to: number;        // offset just past the last matched char
+  text: string;      // full text of the matched line
+  line: number;      // zero-based line index
+  score: number;
+  positions: number[]; // absolute offset of each matched char
+}
+```
+
+```ts
+import { findFuzzyMatches } from "@floatboat/nexus-plugin-search";
+
+const doc = editor.getDocument();
+for (const match of findFuzzyMatches(doc, "todo")) {
+  console.log(`line ${match.line}: ${match.text} (score ${match.score})`);
+}
+```
+
+An empty query returns `[]` (matching `findSearchMatches`), not every line.
+
+### `fuzzyFilter(items, query, options?): FuzzyFilterResult<T>[]`
+
+Rank an arbitrary list of candidates — the building block for a quick-open
+dialog, command palette, or symbol picker. Non-matching items are dropped; the
+rest are ranked best-first, ties broken by original order. Pass `key` to match
+against a field of object items, and `limit` to cap the result count.
+
+```ts
+import { fuzzyFilter } from "@floatboat/nexus-plugin-search";
+
+// strings
+fuzzyFilter(["src/live-preview.ts", "src/fuzzy.ts", "README.md"], "fzy");
+// [{ item: "src/fuzzy.ts", text: "src/fuzzy.ts", score, positions: [4, 6, 8] }]
+
+// objects, via `key`
+const commands = [
+  { id: "bold", title: "Toggle Bold" },
+  { id: "code", title: "Insert Code Block" }
+];
+fuzzyFilter(commands, "tb", { key: (c) => c.title, limit: 10 });
+// ranked by title; each result carries the original `item`
+```
+
+Unlike `findFuzzyMatches`, an **empty query returns every item** (input order,
+score 0) — a picker shows the full list before the user types. `positions`
+index into each result's own `text`.
+
+### Scoring model
+
+The scorer follows fzf's `FuzzyMatchV1`: a forward + backward scan narrows the
+text to the shortest window that still contains the query, then a single linear
+pass scores it. Ranking is shaped by:
+
+| Signal | Effect |
+|---|---|
+| Contiguous run | Adjacent matched characters score higher than scattered ones. |
+| Word boundary | Matching the start of a word (after whitespace / `-`, `_`, `/`, `.`) is rewarded. |
+| camelCase / number boundary | `fooBar` matches `fb` strongly; `v2` rewards the `2`. |
+| First character | Boundary bonuses count double on the query's first character. |
+| Gaps | Unmatched characters between matches are penalized (gap-open + gap-extend). |
+
+### Limits
+
+- **Line-scoped.** `findFuzzyMatches` matches within a single line — a fuzzy
+  match never spans a newline. This keeps results and offsets meaningful for an
+  editor.
+- **Not wired into the `Cmd/Ctrl-F` panel.** `@codemirror/search` has no fuzzy
+  mode, and grafting one in is a separate concern. Fuzzy matching ships as a
+  utility so hosts can build a dedicated finder (quick-open dialog, command
+  palette) on top of it.
+- Offsets are UTF-16 code-unit indices, consistent with CodeMirror document
+  positions.
+

+
+MIT
